title: Fleet Provisioner Service (fleet-provisioner)
author: Ethan Park
body:
## Overview
Fleet Provisioner (`fleet-provisioner`) is an internal control-plane service that orchestrates end-to-end Dedicated capacity bring-up from request to “Ready”. It coordinates infrastructure provisioning, node imaging, cluster bootstrap, configuration validation, readiness checks, and the final Ready state transition that makes a pool eligible for routing.

This service is the system-of-record for provisioning run state and timing, and it is the primary automation surface used by:
- Infra Fleet & Capacity (operators + automation)
- SRE (readiness gates + safe rollout)
- Platform Control Plane/Routing (Ready semantics + capacity advertisement)

**Primary objective:** Reduce “time-to-ready” and operational variance by making provisioning workflows repeatable, observable, and safe-by-default.

## Ownership and on-call
**Owning team:** Platform Control Plane (Eng Platform)
- Engineering owner: Ethan Park (EM, Control Plane)
- Tech lead (routing integration): Ravi Menon

**Operational partners:**
- Fleet automation: Vanessa Ortiz
- SRE readiness/safety: Rafael Mendes

**On-call:**
- Primary: `#eng-platform-oncall` (Control Plane)
- Secondary/escalation: `#eng-infra-oncall` (Fleet) and `#eng-sre-oncall` (SRE)

## What Fleet Provisioner does (and does not do)
### In scope
- Persist and enforce the provisioning run **state machine**.
- Trigger and coordinate stage executors (Terraform apply, imaging hooks, Helm bootstrap, validation, perf-canary).
- Implement **retries/backoff**, cancellation, pause/resume, and partial stage re-run.
- Emit **structured events** and stage timing metrics for observability.
- Drive the authoritative Ready transition used by Routing (only Ready pools are routable).

### Out of scope
- Performing the underlying Terraform or Helm operations directly (delegated to executors/tools).
- Replacing procurement/vendor workflows.
- UI for self-serve customer provisioning (operator CLI and APIs only).

## Key concepts
### Pool
A Dedicated capacity unit represented in the control plane (e.g., customer pool). Pools have a desired configuration and an operational lifecycle.

### Provisioning Run
A single orchestration attempt to bring a pool to Ready. Runs are immutable records with a unique `run_id`, correlation IDs, and audited state transitions.

### Stage
A unit of work within a provisioning run. Stages are run sequentially by default and can be re-run (with guardrails) when safe.

## State machine
Fleet Provisioner enforces the following high-level provisioning states:

Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready

Terminal states:
- Failed
- Canceled

Control states:
- Paused (run-level; preserves current stage state)

### State semantics
- **Provisioning:** Infrastructure created/expanded and base networking/IAM/instances are in place.
- **Imaging:** Nodes are on an approved golden image (or have completed the imaging/hardening step), with drivers and prerequisites pinned.
- **Bootstrapping:** Cluster components are installed (e.g., CNI, node agents, runtime chart prerequisites) and the pool is registered with the control plane.
- **Validating:** Readiness gates and perf-canary readiness suite completed successfully.
- **Ready:** Pool is eligible for routing advertisement and can receive production traffic.

### Routing contract (important)
Routing MUST treat only `Ready` capacity as usable.
- `Validating` is **not** routable.
- The transition to `Ready` is guarded by an atomic “all gates passed + perf-canary completed” check.

## Architecture (high level)
Fleet Provisioner is implemented as a control-plane API + worker model:
- **API layer** receives provisioning requests, validates authz, creates runs, and exposes run status.
- **Orchestrator/worker** evaluates run state, schedules stages, handles retries/backoff, and records transitions.
- **Persistence** stores run/stage records, inputs/outputs, and audit logs.
- **Event emitter** publishes structured provisioning events for observability + Slack bot notifications.

### Dependencies / integrations
- **Terraform orchestration wrapper** (redwood-terraform modules + standardized outputs)
- **Golden image catalog** (approved image versions + signing/provenance)
- **Helm/Bootstrap executor** (pinned chart versions, bootstrap hooks)
- **Config validation service/library** (schema + policy gates + break-glass auditing)
- **Perf-canary readiness suite** (lightweight benchmark + pass/fail JSON)
- **Observability stack** (metrics, logs, dashboards, alerting)

## API
All APIs are internal-only and require service-to-service auth or operator tokens. Endpoints below are the stable interface used by the operator CLI.

### Authentication and authorization
- Service-to-service calls use Redwood internal mTLS + workload identity.
- Operator actions use an operator token with RBAC roles.

Roles:
- `fleet.provisioner.operator`: trigger runs, view status, re-run safe stages
- `fleet.provisioner.admin`: pause/resume, cancel, use break-glass flags, override policy gates (audited)

All mutating actions emit an audit record.

### Idempotency
Mutating requests support `Idempotency-Key` header. Repeated requests with the same key return the original result (when safe).

### Endpoints
| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | /v1/provisioning-runs | Create a run for a pool (new bring-up or expansion) |
| GET | /v1/provisioning-runs/{run_id} | Fetch run summary + stage statuses |
| GET | /v1/provisioning-runs?pool_id=… | List recent runs for a pool |
| POST | /v1/provisioning-runs/{run_id}/pause | Pause orchestration (admin-only) |
| POST | /v1/provisioning-runs/{run_id}/resume | Resume orchestration (admin-only) |
| POST | /v1/provisioning-runs/{run_id}/cancel | Cancel run; best-effort stop stage execution |
| POST | /v1/provisioning-runs/{run_id}/rerun-stage | Re-run a stage (or subset) with safety checks |
| GET | /v1/pools/{pool_id}/readiness | Current readiness + last run pointer |

### Create run: request/response (example)
Request:
- `POST /v1/provisioning-runs`
- Headers: `Idempotency-Key: 9b0a...`

Body (illustrative):
```json
{
  "pool_id": "ded-9f3c2c",
  "mode": "expand",
  "target_capacity": {"gpus": 64, "sku": "H100-80GB"},
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "config_version": "poolcfg-2025-02-28.3",
  "requested_by": "harish.reddy",
  "notes": "Customer expansion window 02:00-04:00 UTC"
}
```
Response:
```json
{
  "run_id": "prun_01HPYQK5R5F0D6M7JZ7KJ6W7W6",
  "state": "Requested",
  "created_at": "2025-03-02T01:14:22Z",
  "pool_id": "ded-9f3c2c"
}
```

### Re-run stage (example)
`POST /v1/provisioning-runs/{run_id}/rerun-stage`
```json
{
  "stage": "Validating",
  "scope": "stage_only",
  "reason": "Transient DNS failure; infra + bootstrap are healthy",
  "requested_by": "vanessa.ortiz"
}
```
Notes:
- By default, Fleet Provisioner reuses cached outputs from prior stages when safe.
- Some transitions require an explicit admin override if the stage is not considered safe to rerun without re-provisioning.

## Events
Fleet Provisioner emits structured events to the Redwood Event Bus for:
- dashboards (stage timing, failure modes)
- alerting (stuck stage, high failure rate)
- Slack status updates (via incident-bot integration)

### Event types
| Event | Emitted when |
|---|---|
| fleet.provisioning.run.created | Run record created |
| fleet.provisioning.run.state_changed | Run-level state transitions |
| fleet.provisioning.stage.started | Stage execution begins |
| fleet.provisioning.stage.succeeded | Stage completed successfully |
| fleet.provisioning.stage.failed | Stage failed (includes error classification) |
| fleet.provisioning.run.paused | Run paused |
| fleet.provisioning.run.resumed | Run resumed |
| fleet.provisioning.run.canceled | Run canceled |
| fleet.provisioning.run.ready | Pool marked Ready |
| fleet.provisioning.run.failed | Run enters Failed terminal state |

### Common event fields
All events include:
- `run_id`
- `pool_id`
- `region`
- `stage` (if stage event)
- `state` (new state)
- `correlation_id` (propagated through executors)
- `attempt` (retry attempt index)
- `duration_ms` (when applicable)
- `error_category` and `error_code` (on failures)

Event payload (illustrative):
```json
{
  "event_type": "fleet.provisioning.stage.failed",
  "timestamp": "2025-03-02T02:31:10Z",
  "run_id": "prun_01HPYQK5R5F0D6M7JZ7KJ6W7W6",
  "pool_id": "ded-9f3c2c",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "stage": "Imaging",
  "attempt": 2,
  "duration_ms": 128403,
  "correlation_id": "corr_7c2b6d5d2c3e",
  "error_category": "ARTIFACT_MIRROR",
  "error_code": "IMAGE_PULL_TIMEOUT",
  "message": "Timed out downloading golden image artifact from mirror; will retry with alternate mirror"
}
```

## Retry and backoff policy
Retries are stage-specific and are designed to be:
- safe (idempotent operations when possible)
- bounded (avoid infinite loops)
- observable (attempt counts + final error surfaced)

### Default retry policy
| Stage | Max attempts | Backoff | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Provisioning | 3 | exponential (30s → 5m) | Terraform wrapper must be idempotent; detects partial applies |
| Imaging | 4 | exponential (1m → 10m) | Supports alternate mirror fallback; detects SKU/region hot spots |
| Bootstrapping | 3 | exponential (1m → 8m) | Helm installs/updates must be safe; avoids double-registration |
| Validating | 2 | fixed (2m) | Avoid masking real failures; prefer operator investigation |

### Failure classification (used for alerts + runbook routing)
Fleet Provisioner normalizes failures into categories:
- `QUOTA_OR_CAPACITY` (cloud quota, unavailable SKU)
- `IAM_OR_PERMISSIONS`
- `NETWORKING` (DNS, routing, TLS, SG/NACL)
- `ARTIFACT_MIRROR` (image pulls, registry failures)
- `GPU_HEALTH` (ECC, missing GPU, driver mismatch)
- `HELM_VALUES_OR_CONFIG` (invalid values, missing required fields)
- `PERF_CANARY_REGRESSION` (fails thresholds)
- `UNKNOWN`

## Configuration and validation
Fleet Provisioner does not define the pool config schema itself; it consumes the validated output of the Config Validation library/policy gates.

### Validation gates
Before entering `Bootstrapping`:
- config schema validation must pass
- policy gates must pass (e.g., pinned chart versions, disallowed flags)

Break-glass:
- Admin-only override is available for specific policies.
- Every break-glass action creates an audit log entry and emits an event (`fleet.provisioning.policy.break_glass_used`).

## Observability
### Metrics
Fleet Provisioner emits:
- `fleet_time_to_ready_seconds` (overall)
- `fleet_stage_duration_seconds{stage=...}`
- `fleet_stage_attempts_total{stage=..., outcome=...}`
- `fleet_runs_total{outcome=..., region=..., sku=...}`
- `fleet_stuck_stage_total{stage=...}` (derived)

Cardinality guardrails:
- `pool_id` is not used as a default metric label; use logs/events for per-pool drilldowns.
- Dashboards query per-pool using event streams and run IDs.

### Logs
Structured logs include:
- `run_id`, `pool_id`, `stage`, `attempt`, `correlation_id`
- executor references (terraform apply ID, helm release name, perf-canary run ID)

### Dashboards and alerts
See: **Dedicated Readiness Dashboard Spec** and **Time-to-ready metrics and alerting** pages.

Standard alerts:
- Stage stuck beyond budget (warning → ticket; paging only for production pilots / high-severity)
- High failure rate for a stage by region/SKU
- Break-glass usage (always creates a ticket + Slack notification)

## Data model (conceptual)
Fleet Provisioner stores:
- provisioning runs (run metadata, desired inputs, actor)
- stage execution records (timestamps, attempts, outputs pointers)
- audit log (who did what, when)

Outputs are stored by reference (e.g., object store pointers, executor run IDs) rather than embedding large artifacts.

## Operational notes
### Safety properties
- A pool cannot transition to `Ready` unless all required gates pass.
- Re-run operations are denied if they would violate state safety (unless admin override).
- Cancellation attempts to stop outstanding tasks and leaves the run in `Canceled` with clear operator guidance for cleanup.

### Manual override and operator workflows
- Preferred: re-run stage after mitigation (e.g., fix IAM permission, correct Helm values).
- If partial automation is required, operators may:
  - pause the run
  - execute a manual remediation
  - resume the run and re-run the appropriate stage

### Known pitfalls / guardrails
- Helm values drift can cause bootstrap loops; drift detection is enabled to surface mismatch between intended vs actual.
- Imaging timeouts are frequently mirror-related; fallback logic is enabled and will annotate events with mirror chosen.
- Perf-canary must complete before Ready (enforced; do not bypass without explicit approval).

## Runbook links
- Dedicated pool provisioning runbook: prerequisites, commands, rollbacks
- Control-plane Ready troubleshooting: “infra up but not Ready” cases
- Image build and rollout runbook: golden image promotion + rollback

## Change management
- Significant changes to state machine, retry policy, or Ready semantics require:
  - an ADR update (or new ADR)
  - SRE review of alerting impact
  - staged rollout behind a feature flag

## Appendix A: Stage definitions (executor responsibilities)
### Provisioning (Terraform)
- Inputs: pool config, region, SKU, target capacity
- Outputs: cluster endpoints, node group IDs, networking outputs, IAM roles

### Imaging
- Inputs: desired golden image version, node group IDs
- Outputs: imaging success, image provenance attestations (pointers)

### Bootstrapping
- Inputs: cluster endpoint, pinned helm chart versions, bootstrap hooks
- Outputs: helm release versions, registration status, component health summary

### Validating
- Checks: DNS, TLS, network egress, GPU health, runtime smoke test, perf-canary readiness suite
- Outputs: pass/fail + summary JSON pointer, threshold details
